claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory alloys for fusion plasma-facing components are largely governed by severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion alters dislocation core structures.
Lattice distortion forces edge dislocations to adopt wavy, non-planar configurations.
Wavy, non-planar edge dislocations have reduced mobility and promote uniform, strain-hardening deformation.
NbTaTiV-type refractory high-entropy alloy can exhibit a single BCC solid-solution phase stable through 900 °C.
The initial NbTaTiV-type alloy is a random solid solution with significant compositional lattice distortion.
Higher configurational complexity produces higher lattice distortion, whereas limited compositional variance minimizes lattice distortion.
NbTaTiV has been mechanically tested at 700–900 °C under a controlled strain rate.
Random atomic distributions generate local lattice distortion that perturbs dislocation core structures.
Deviation of dislocation cores from ideal slip planes increases the energy barrier for kink-pair nucleation.
An increased kink-pair nucleation barrier lowers dislocation mobility.
Lower dislocation mobility enhances strain hardening and makes elevated-temperature plastic deformation more uniform.
More uniform plastic deformation delays localized failure and promotes toughness.
Relative to a low-distortion control, the high-distortion alloy will have lower dislocation mobility, a higher strain-hardening rate, and greater high-temperature ductility and toughness.
The high-distortion alloy may have slightly lower yield strength than the control because of a trade-off with strengthening mechanisms.
A low-randomness control should exhibit more screw-dislocation activity or planar slip, lower strain hardening, and reduced toughness.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold at approximately 700–900 °C under fusion-service-relevant strain rates when oxidation and irradiation effects are negligible.
The quantitative distortion effect may be confounded by grain size, secondary phases, and irradiation-induced defects.
A failure to observe both decreased dislocation mobility and increased strain hardening and toughness after increasing lattice distortion would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The design requires identical overall composition while also proposing fewer principal elements as a way to create the low-randomness alloy. Reducing the number of principal elements necessarily changes the overall composition, so that example cannot satisfy the stated identical-composition control.
